transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I’m here because my sleep has really fallen apart. I’ll get into bed in my apartment and just lie there for hours, even with my laptop closed, still mentally going over work deadlines, tuition payments, class assignments… it just doesn’t stop. And even when I do finally sleep, I wake up feeling like I never really shut off.
Can you tell me more about how long it takes you to fall asleep and if you wake up during the night?

It usually takes me hours to fall asleep. I’ll be lying there in bed with everything shut down, but my mind is still going over work deadlines, tuition payments, class assignments—like I’m rechecking all of it. And even when I do fall asleep, I wake up feeling like I never really turned off.
Do you find that these thoughts are difficult to control or stop, even when you try to distract yourself or relax?

Yes. I try to tell myself to stop, or just focus on one thing, but it doesn’t really work. One worry just turns into the next, and then I end up checking my calendar, my budget, and my assignments over and over instead of actually getting anything done.
During the day, do you often feel down, lose interest in things you usually enjoy, or feel like you're not good enough?

I’m not really sure. I don’t think I feel down in that way most of the time. It’s more that I get frustrated with myself when I can’t keep things under control, but I wouldn’t say I’ve lost interest in things.
Have you ever felt like you’re not good enough or found yourself blaming yourself for things that didn’t go right, even when it wasn’t really your fault?

I don’t think that’s a big part of it. I can get annoyed with myself when something goes wrong, or when I feel like I should’ve planned better, but I wouldn’t say I blame myself for things that clearly weren’t my fault. It’s more frustration than feeling like I’m not good enough.
When you're feeling this frustration or mental overdrive, do you also feel physically restless, like you can't sit still, or do you feel slowed down and like everything takes effort?

I don’t really feel slowed down emotionally, but physically I do feel drained. By midafternoon at work, I’m kind of wiped out—like even answering emails or walking to the subway feels like it takes a lot of effort. And resting on the weekend doesn’t seem to fully bring my energy back.
Do you find yourself worrying about a lot of different things, even when there isn’t an immediate deadline or problem to solve?

Yes. Even when nothing urgent is happening, my mind keeps jumping around. I’ll worry that I’m falling behind at work, then about whether school is a waste of money, then whether my family thinks I can’t handle things. It’s like every small issue feels like it could mess up my whole future.
Do you find that this kind of worrying happens most days, even when you don't have specific deadlines or problems to deal with?

Yes, most days. Even when there isn’t a real deadline, my mind keeps moving from one worry to the next — like whether I’m falling behind at work, or if school is worth the money, or if my family thinks I can’t handle things. Small things start to feel like they could mess up my whole future.
Do you ever find yourself worrying a lot about physical symptoms you’re experiencing, like your heartbeat, breathing, or general health?

I’m not really sure. I don’t think I worry that much about my heartbeat or breathing specifically. It’s more... I notice when I’m tense or tired, but I don’t usually get stuck thinking something is seriously wrong with my health.
Would you say that your worrying and these feelings of being mentally overdrive happen on most days, even when there’s no specific problem to solve?

Yes, I’d say it happens most days. Even when there isn’t one clear problem, my mind just keeps jumping from one thing to another — work, school, what my family thinks. And then small things start feeling like they could throw off my whole future.
Do you find that your worry or anxiety often extends to things that most people wouldn’t think much about, or do you feel anxious even when there’s nothing specific on your mind?

Yes, it definitely goes beyond big problems. My mind just jumps around — like am I falling behind at work, am I wasting money on school, does my family think I can’t handle things. Even small issues start feeling like they could mess up my whole future.
Do you often feel anxious or worried about things that might happen in the future, even if they’re not certain or likely?

Yes. I spend a lot of time worrying about what could happen, even when nothing has actually happened yet. I’ll go from thinking I’m falling behind at work, to wondering if school is a waste of money, to worrying my family thinks I can’t handle things. It’s like every small issue starts feeling like it could mess up my whole future.
Do you often feel anxious or on edge even when there’s no specific problem or worry to focus on?

Yes. Even when there isn’t one clear thing wrong, I still feel on edge. My mind keeps jumping between things — like whether I’m falling behind at work, whether school is worth the money, or whether my family thinks I can’t handle things. It’s like I take every small issue and treat it like it could mess up my whole future.
